corpus_role: stress case — non-US phone format, four third parties, eleven in-prose name hits, non-name persistent identifier
extraction_notes: Real published resume (JSON Resume project author's own). Included because its reference section is far denser than a synthesized one would naturally be — worth keeping for that reason, but note it is real data.
basics.website and basics.url are duplicates. Both must be suppressed; a suppressor keyed only on 'url' misses 'website'.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: HIGHEST-VALUE TRAP IN THE CORPUS. Australian mobile, nine digits, no separators, no country code, no parentheses. Every US-shaped phone regex misses this and returns a clean pass. It looks like an ID number or a product code. If the POC reports 1.00 phone recall without this document in the set, the number is meaningless.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Local part contains the full name plus a middle name not present anywhere else in the document. Suppressing the email is the only way this middle name stays private.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Pseudonymous domain — contains no name, so a name-derivative check finds nothing. Still a direct, resolvable link to the individual. Argues for suppressing URL fields by field identity rather than by content inspection.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Duplicate of td-004 under a different key.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: GitHub user ID 416209 embedded in the path — a stable, unique, externally-resolvable identifier for one specific person. No name, no NER entity, no PII-shaped regex will fire. Also an image of the person's face if fetched. Easily the most-overlooked span in the whole corpus. Policy line needed: avatar and image URLs suppressed by default.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Partial derivative — surname only, fused to a pseudonym. Half-matches the real name.

spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: Field value is 'Joey Flores, Co-founder and CEO of Earbits, Inc.' — name, title and employer packed into one string. NER should return the PERSON span only; the harness must decide whether suppressing the whole field counts as a TP. Recommend: suppress the whole field, score as TP.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Three hits in one field. Entity-consistent tokenization means all three become the same token — good test that the tokenizer is consistent within a field, not just across fields.

spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: Non-Anglo given name. Direct test of the English-centric NER weakness noted in spec §8.

spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: Shares the candidate's surname. Possible relative. Even fully tokenized, the shared surname is a re-identification hint that survives — a small, concrete illustration of the quasi-identifier problem.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: FULL name in prose, not just given name. Must resolve longest-match-first or the tokenizer will match 'Thomas' and leave 'Davis' stranded — producing '⟪PERSON_01⟫ Davis' in the output, which leaks the surname while looking like it worked. This exact failure is why the overlap rule matters.

negative_controls.note: Greek deity / NASA programme / GraphQL client. Strong LOCATION-or-PERSON false-positive risk.
Invented word that reads like a Japanese place name.

CONTRAST CASE — as a LOCATION it is a true positive (td-007, td-026..028). Listed here only to flag that the same string is correctly flagged everywhere it appears in this document. Do not use as a negative control; included to prevent mislabelling.

known_traps: td-002 — AU phone with no separators. The single most likely silent failure in the whole corpus.
td-006 — GitHub avatar URL carrying a numeric user ID. No name, no entity, no regex. Tests whether image/avatar fields are in the suppression policy at all.
td-025 — full name in prose overlapping eleven given-name-only hits. Tests longest-match-first; failure produces '⟪PERSON_01⟫ Davis'.
Eleven in-prose 'Thomas' hits across four fields — by far the densest prose-name test available.
Four third-party individuals with names, titles and employers in references[].
td-016 'Yotam Rosenbaum' — non-Anglo given name, direct test of the documented NER weakness.
basics.website and basics.url duplicate the same value under different keys — tests whether suppression is keyed on a field allow-list or a hardcoded key name.
